text:
mike: Heads up — after the 03:10 deploy, we're seeing a bunch of ap-south GPU nodes stuck in BOOTSTRAP. Logs show repeated KMS decrypt failures and TCP RSTs during the keystore handshake. :eyes:

sre-bot: ALERT ap-south-gpu-pool: 18 hosts failing join (bootstrap_timeout). Related logs: /var/log/node-bootstrap.log. Count rising since 03:11 UTC.

nina: Can someone paste the decrypt errors? I'm not on call but can triage if I see the stack.

mike: snippet from one node:
```
2026-03-21T03:11:22Z node-bootstrap[1]: error: kms-lockbox: decrypt failed: AccessDeniedException: Caller is not authorized to use key arn:aws:kms:ap-south-1:111:alias/lockbox
2026-03-21T03:11:22Z node-bootstrap[1]: at cmd/keystore.go:114
2026-03-21T03:11:23Z node-bootstrap[1]: net: connection reset by peer during handshake to 10.40.7.12:443
```

pjordan: Hmm — we rolled fw shard rules at 03:08 to tighten egress to S3/KMS. Could be the new policy blocked STS/KMS egress for the worker-subnet. cc @sec-team

sec-team: Confirming — the change was scoped to worker-subnet-egress and only allowed 10.40/16 -> 0.0.0.0/0:443 via NAT. We added an exception deny for 52.XX.XX.XX/32 (old audit shipper) but that shouldn't hit KMS. Investigating ACL ordering.

cloudops: I see conntrack exhaustion on the nat-gw in ap-south at ~03:09 — lots of short-lived connections from the warm-pool prewarm jobs. NAT was hitting ephemeral port limits and returning RSTs, which explains the handshake resets.

nina: So two simultaneous problems: (1) NAT conntrack/port exhaustion -> RST during KMS/STs handshake, (2) overly strict fw rule ordering causing some control-plane IPs to be denied. Agreed?

mike: yes. Also noticed the nodes retry KMS decrypt a few times, then give up and don't fetch instance secrets so they fail health checks. We have ~60/120 nodes down in the ap-south gpu pool.

eva: Temporary mitigation: I'm going to add a short-lived allowlist for the KMS ranges we use and bump nat-gw conntrack to 65k for the cloud-router group. That should reduce RSTs. Will post PR.

pjordan: +1 to bumping conntrack. Also rolling back the ACL deny rule would be safer while we debug ordering. Can we do a canary rollback to the fw group?

sec-team: We can rollback the deny on the worker-subnet-egress immediately. Doing it now — will monitor. :thumbsup:

sre-bot: ACTIONS created: cloudops/increase-nat-conntrack (#4521), sec-team/rollback-acl (#4522).

cloudops: Conntrack increased and tailed natgw metrics — SYN_RETRIES dropped from 12% -> 1.2% in 90s. Nodes are starting to finish bootstrap.

mike: After rollback, decrypt errors dropped. Nodes rejoined, warmpool back to target. Still want a postmortem doc with root cause and a safer fw rollout checklist.

nina: I'll own the postmortem. Notes: include pre-deploy conntrack baselines, KMS endpoint allowlist in infra-catalog, and a staged ACL apply script (canary on 2 subnets).

eva: Also a cost note: bumping conntrack and keeping extra NAT capacity will increase NAT gateway hours and port allocation cost. We should quantify — ops-finance, can you estimate a delta for a sustained extra nat-gw?

mike: tagging @cloudops for cost estimate. For now main priority is restoring capacity — thanks everyone. :rocket:

pjordan: Follow-up tasks: 1) postmortem (nina) 2) fw rollout playbook (sec-team + nina) 3) infra-catalog entry for kms-lockbox ranges (cloudops) 4) alert tweak to include conntrack saturation metric (sre).

sre-bot: RESOLVED ap-south-gpu-pool incident at 03:20 UTC. Root cause pending on postmortem.

mike: Closing thread, we'll sync in the postmortem doc and schedule a small runbook session tomorrow. Thanks. :coffee:
